title: Chocolate-almond fat bombs
summary: Small frozen bites of almond butter, coconut oil and cocoa with a little chopped almond for crunch.
steps: Set 16 silicone mini-muffin cups or candy moulds on a small tray that fits in your freezer.
Melt the coconut oil and almond butter together in a small pan over low heat, stirring, just until fluid. Do not let it get hot.
Take the pan off the heat and whisk in the cocoa, powdered erythritol, vanilla and salt until no lumps of cocoa remain.
Divide among the moulds, about 1 tablespoon each, and scatter the chopped almonds over the tops.
Freeze for at least 1 hour, until hard, then pop them out and store in a sealed container.
tips: Coconut oil melts at about 24 °C (76 °F), so keep these in the freezer or fridge and eat them cold.
Stir the mixture once more just before pouring; the cocoa settles as it stands.

origin.history: Fat bombs are a modern invention, not a traditional sweet. They grew out of the ketogenic and low-carb diet communities in the United States in the 2010s, where home cooks shared recipes for small, sugar-free, high-fat snacks built on coconut oil, nut butters and cocoa. This flavour borrows from the much older pairing of chocolate and almond.
